Meaning: v. to put someone or something in danger
Example: A hot stove can imperil your fingers if you touch it without caution.

Meaning: v. to be at risk of great harm or death
Example: Animal species that are endangered might disappear from the planet forever.

Meaning: v. to make sure that something is kept
Example: We use a special jar to preserve fruits and make delicious jams.

Meaning: v. to stop something from being done or used, especially by law
Example: The sign says "No Pets Allowed" to prohibit animals in the store.

Meaning: v. to be aware that something exists or is true
Example: I can easily recognize my friend's voice on the phone.

Meaning: v. to persuade someone to do something
Example: I'll try to convince my parents to let me stay up a bit later tonight.

Meaning: v. to separate the solid part from the liquid part
Example: I strain the pasta to remove the water after cooking it.

Meaning: v. to add a harmful substance to something
Example: Throwing garbage into the river can contaminate the water.

Meaning: n. an area of land where the animals, birds, and plants are officially protected
Example: The park has a nature reserve where animals are protected.

Meaning: adj. kind, helpful and generous
Example: Our school organized a benevolent event to raise money for charity.

Meaning:
v. 1. To have or to find room for.
2. To do a favor for.
Example:
1. This bus, which accommodates thirty adults, will drive to the historic buildings in the center of the city.
2. Tell me what you want, and I will try to accommodate you.

Meaning:
adj. 1. Ready to attack or start fights; acting in a hostile way.
2. Bold and active.
Example:
1. Many animals become aggressive when their young are threatened.
2. Serena Williams, the American tennis star, plays a talented and aggressive game.

Meaning:
v. 1. To relax where it is pleasantly warm.
2. To enjoy a warm or pleasant feeling.
Example:
1. At lunch break, several students basked in the sunshine flooding the front steps.
2. The twins basked in the praise heaped on them by their parents.

Meaning: n. The dead body of an animal.
Example: We called the city to request that the raccoon carcass on our street be removed.

Meaning: v. To keep something or someone from being seen or known; to hide.
Example: Playing hide-and-seek with my younger cousins, I concealed myself behind the kitchen door.

Meaning: v. To strike out or swing wildly; to thrash about.
Example: Matt's arms flailed desperately after he jumped in the pool.

Meaning:
n. A narrow passage between steep cliffs.
v. To stuff with food; to eat greedily.
Example:
n. We crossed the gorge on a swaying rope bridge.
v. The children gorged themselves on watermelon at the family picnic.

Meaning: n. A small amount, especially of something good to eat; a tidbit.
Example: For appetizers we served stuffed mushrooms and other tasty morsels.

Meaning: v. To stick out; to project.
Example: Watch out for the stone ledge that protrudes from the wall.

Meaning:
v. To form small waves.
n. A movement like a small wave.
Example:
v. The breeze rippled the surface of the lake.
n. Raindrops made ripples in the pond.

Meaning: v. To move with a sliding, side-to-side motion of the body.
Example: A snake slithered through the grass.

Meaning:
adj. 1. Lacking energy; not active.
2. Slow moving.
Example:
1. The heat made me sluggish.
2. In the dry season, the river becomes little more than a sluggish stream.

Meaning: n. The nose or jaws that stick out in front of certain animals' heads.
Example: The snout of a crocodile is full of long, sharp teeth.

Meaning:
v. 1. To make or become less wide or less thick at one end.
2. To lessen gradually. (Usually used with off.)
n. A thin candle.
Example:
1. The little dog's tail tapers to a point.
2. When a loud knock was heard at the door, the professor's voice tapered off until she fell silent.
n. The only light in the room came from a flickering taper.

Meaning: adj. Able to be seen; exposed to view; not hidden.
Example: On a clear day Mount Shasta is visible from fifty miles away.

Meaning: n. a long and difficult attempt to achieve something
Example: Life became a struggle for survival.

Meaning: n. the regular light work of a household or farm
Example: Cleaning my room and washing the dishes are some of my chores.

Meaning: n. a fun act, such as a dance or party
Example: All of us enjoy nice frolics in the meadow on a warm spring day.

Meaning: adj. bending the top part of your body forward and raising your shoulders and back
Example: The hunched over man looked like he was in pain.

Meaning: v. to keep moving your body, hands, or feet
Example: Sit still and stop fidgeting!

Meaning: v. to complain about someone or something in a bad-tempered way
Example: They kept grumbling that they were cold.

Meaning: n. the short, stiff stalks of plants that remain in a field after harvesting
Example: After the tractor moved across the field, all that was left of the corn plants were rows of stubble.

Meaning: adj. necessary
Example: The mayor needed to prove that he was indispensable by solving the city's big problems.

Meaning: v. to get rid of a thirst by drinking liquid
Example: He stopped to quench his thirst at a stream.

Meaning: v. to move in a slow, heavy, and awkward way
Example: The elephant lumbered through the forest.

Meaning: adj. delicate or small
Example: The bee landed on the dainty petals of the flower.

Meaning: n. a manner of moving heavily and slowly
Example: We watched the horse's slow plod through the snow.

Meaning: adj. not willing to accept change, help, or control
Example: My little brother can be stubborn when he doesn't want to eat his vegetables.

Meaning: adj. unaware of something
Example: He was oblivious to the person behind him.

Meaning: n. the size or shape of something
Example: The proportions of the furniture fit the size of the dollhouse perfectly.

Meaning: v. to entertain someone with stories or jokes
Example: Chen regaled his family with funny stories about her day.

Meaning: v. to gather crops that are ripe
Example: The farmers harvested the ripe corn from the field.

Meaning: n. land that is covered or mostly covered with grass
Example: The meadow was filled with colorful wildflowers and buzzing bees.

Meaning: v. to beat a plant in order to separate its grain or seeds from the rest of the plant
Example: Neighbors often helped one another thresh the wheat.

Meaning: n. a guess or estimate about something that will happen in the future
Example: Mom checked the forecast to decide what clothes to wear.

Meaning:
n. 1. Freedom or permission to enter.
2. A way of approach or entry.
Example:
1. The students want access to the gym this summer.
2. The only access to the harbor is this channel.

Meaning:
v. 1. To bring together in the mind.
2. To come or be together as friends or companions.
n. A person with whom one is connected in some way, as in business.
Example:
1. Many people associate Florida with oranges.
2. Because of her love of racehorses, Anne often associated with others who shared that love—jockeys and trainers.
n. My father discussed a project with his associate at work.

Meaning: adj. Noisy and uncontrolled.
Example: The Dixons' party became so boisterous that their neighbors complained.

Meaning:
adj. 1. Very bright; sparkling.
2. Very clever or smart.
Example:
1. My black leather shoes had a brilliant shine.
2. My oldest sister is so brilliant she might finish high school in three years.

Meaning: n. A ten-year period.
Example: I have hope that the next decade will be better than the last.

Meaning:
adj. 1. Easily broken or damaged.
2. Needing care and skill.
3. In poor health; weak.
Example:
1. We always wash this delicate antique plate by hand.
2. Convincing small children to share a toy can be a delicate task.
3. Although Isabella Bird Bishop was a delicate child, as an adult, she traveled through many different parts of the world, sometimes by canoe and other times on horseback.

Meaning:
v. 1. To hire and put to work for pay.
2. To use.
Example:
1. Carmen's gift shop employs four people.
2. The clown employed every trick he knew to make the children laugh.

Meaning:
adj. Doing nothing; not working.
v. 1. To spend one's time doing nothing.
2. To run (an engine) slowly.
Example:
adj. The workers were idle while the power was shut off.
v. 1. Last Sunday, while my brother idled for more than an hour in the house, I raked leaves in the yard.
v. 2. Let the car idle for a few minutes so that the engine can warm up.

Meaning:
v. 1. To light up; to supply with light.
2. To make clear or understandable.
Example:
1. The full moon illuminated the path through the woods to our cabin.
2. The teacher's explanation illuminated the math problem for me.

Meaning:
v. 1. To give what is needed; to supply.
2. To set forth as a condition.
Example:
1. Two local companies provided the money to buy our school band uniforms.
2. Our agreement with the teacher provides for a party if we turn our work in on time all year.

Meaning: v. To need or demand.
Example: Plants require light and water in order to grow.

Meaning:
v. To make fun of in an insulting way; to jeer.
n. An insulting remark.
Example:
v. Don't taunt someone just because that person appears different.
n. An umpire learns to ignore the taunts of the crowd and just get on with the job.

Meaning: adj. Willing to let others have their own beliefs and ways, even if different from one's own.
Example: Traveling is both interesting and enjoyable if you are tolerant of customs that seem strange to you.

Meaning: v. To change the form, looks, or nature of.
Example: A fresh coat of paint will transform this room.

Meaning: n. An area where there are few people living; an area still in its natural state.
Example: The Rocky Mountain states contain large areas of wilderness.

Meaning: n. Something that causes great damage or harm.
Example: Hurricane Katrina was the worst disaster to hit New Orleans in many years.

Meaning: v. To run away from danger or from something frightening.
Example: I quickly decided to flee from the park when I heard a noise behind me.

Meaning:
n. A crack or break, as in metal or bone.
v. To crack or break.
Example:
n. The plane was grounded because of a small fracture in the metal tail unit.
v. Selena fractured her arm for the second time this summer when she fell from the swing.

Meaning:
adj. 1. Great in size or extent.
2. Great in degree.
Example:
1. The Pacific Ocean is an immense body of water.
2. To the immense relief of his parents, the lost child was soon found.

Meaning:
adj. 1. Very strong; very great.
2. Showing great depth of feeling.
Example:
1. The intense heat from the fire melted the plastic dishes.
2. The scene in the play where the enslaved people are liberated from bondage is so intense that the audience often weeps.

Meaning: v. To look into closely; to study in great detail.
Example: The fire marshal will investigate the cause of the fire in the library.

Meaning:
v. To move forward or to one side suddenly and unexpectedly.
n. A jerking or swaying movement.
Example:
v. The car lurched to the left to avoid a bird on the road.
n. The bus started with a lurch, throwing the standing passengers off balance.

Meaning:
adj. Great in size, number, or importance.
v. To study as one's most important subject.
Example:
adj. Seas and oceans make up the major part of the earth's surface.
v. My cousin Karen majored in chemistry and mathematics at Community College.

Meaning:
adj. 1. Small; unimportant.
n. A person who is not yet an adult; a child.
Example:
adj. Steffi's knee injury was minor, so she finished the game.
n. Minors may attend this movie if an adult goes with them.

Meaning:
v. 1. To make rigid with terror; to terrify.
2. To change into a stonelike substance.
Example:
1. The director said that he felt his horror movies had failed if they did not petrify audiences.
2. In Arizona's Painted Desert, we saw examples of wood that had petrified over millions of years.

Meaning: v. To say what will happen before it takes place.
Example: The highway safety office predicts heavy traffic on the roads this weekend.

Meaning:
adj. 1. Likely to have or do.
2. Lying face downward.
Example:
1. All of us are more prone to colds in the winter than in the summer.
2. I had to lie in a prone position because my back was so sunburned.

Meaning:
adj. 1. Thinly grown or spread.
2. Not crowded.
Example:
1. The grass on the ball field was sparse, so we reseeded it.
2. The town meeting had a sparse turnout this year.

Meaning:
v. 1. To fall or push over.
2. To overthrow.
Example:
1. The cat toppled the pile of books.
2. The student demonstrations helped topple the government.

Meaning: adj. Having to do with cities.
Example: Traffic in urban areas is a serious problem during rush hour.
